summary.name: Tactile
summary.one_liner: Tactile is a free, open-source macOS menu-bar app that plays trackpad haptic taps when the cursor passes over clickable elements system-wide.
use_cases: feel when hovering over buttons and links on a Mac
accessibility aid for locating clickable elements
distinguish destructive actions like Delete by stronger haptic feedback
get tactile feedback for keyboard shortcuts
make browser buttons easier to find with the Chrome extension
summary.what_it_does: Tactile runs in the macOS menu bar and triggers trackpad haptic taps whenever the cursor moves over a button, link, menu, or tab in any app, including Finder, browsers, and Electron apps. An optional Chrome extension extends detection to browser buttons the app would otherwise miss. Destructive actions such as Delete and Remove get a distinct, stronger haptic feel. It also offers keyboard ticks for shortcuts and keys, plus visual accessibility aids that follow the cursor: a cursor circle, element highlight, locator lines, and line and label. Haptic waveforms are composable and presets are available.
notable: Haptic taps over every clickable element system-wide, including native apps, Finder, browsers, and Electron
Optional Chrome extension for buttons missed in the browser
Accessibility visual aids: cursor circle, element highlight, locator lines, line and label
Private by design: no network access, no content reading, local only
caveats: Relies on the trackpad haptic engine, so it is only useful on Macs with a haptic trackpad
